## Overview

This notebook explores the DataCo Smart Supply Chain dataset to understand
demand patterns, shipping performance, and product category dynamics before
building the forecasting model. Every finding below is computed from the
warehouse built by `scripts/setup_data.py`.

```{python}
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
from pathlib import Path

# Load plotly.js once from its CDN instead of embedding a copy in every chart
pio.renderers.default = "notebook_connected"

# Connect to the DuckDB warehouse
DB_PATH = str(Path("../data/processed/warehouse.duckdb"))
con = duckdb.connect(DB_PATH, read_only=True)
q = lambda sql: con.execute(sql).fetchdf()
MODEL_END_DATE = "2017-10-02"
```

## Dataset Overview

```{python}
overview = q("""
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_lines,
           COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders,
           COUNT(DISTINCT category_name) AS categories,
           MIN(order_date) AS first_date,
           MAX(order_date) AS last_date,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_valid_demand) AS canceled_or_fraud_lines
    FROM orders
""")
overview.T.rename(columns={0: "value"})
```

## Demand by Category

```{python}
category_demand = q("""
    SELECT
        category_name,
        COUNT(*) AS order_lines,
        SUM(quantity) AS total_units,
        ROUND(SUM(revenue), 0) AS total_revenue,
        ROUND(AVG(unit_price), 2) AS avg_price
    FROM orders
    WHERE is_valid_demand
    GROUP BY category_name
    ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
    LIMIT 15
""")

fig = px.bar(
    category_demand,
    x="total_revenue",
    y="category_name",
    orientation="h",
    title="Revenue by Product Category (Top 15, excluding canceled/fraud)",
    labels={"total_revenue": "Total Revenue ($)", "category_name": "Category"},
)
fig.update_layout(yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"), height=500)
fig.show()
```

## A Structural Break in October 2017

```{python}
monthly = q("""
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
           SUM(total_units) AS units,
           COUNT(DISTINCT category_name) FILTER (WHERE total_units > 0) AS active_categories
    FROM daily_demand
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""")
fig = px.line(monthly, x="month", y="units", title="Monthly Units Sold",
              labels={"month": "", "units": "Units"}, markers=True)
fig.add_vline(x=MODEL_END_DATE, line_dash="dot")
fig.show()

before = monthly[monthly["month"] < "2017-10-01"].tail(6)["units"].mean()
after = monthly[monthly["month"] >= "2017-11-01"]["units"].mean()
print(f"Average monthly units, 6 months before Oct 2017: {before:,.0f}")
print(f"Average monthly units, Nov 2017 – Jan 2018:      {after:,.0f} ({after / before - 1:+.0%})")
```

After 2017-10-02 the catalog changes: most long-running categories stop and a
handful of new ones appear, while total volume falls sharply. Forecasting models
are therefore trained and evaluated only on data up to `MODEL_END_DATE`.

## Is There Weekly Seasonality?

```{python}
weekday = q(f"""
    SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM order_date) AS dow, AVG(units) AS avg_units
    FROM (SELECT order_date, SUM(total_units) AS units
          FROM daily_demand WHERE order_date <= '{MODEL_END_DATE}' GROUP BY 1)
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""")
weekday["day"] = ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"]
spread = weekday["avg_units"].max() / weekday["avg_units"].min() - 1
fig = px.bar(weekday, x="day", y="avg_units", title="Average Daily Units by Weekday",
             labels={"day": "", "avg_units": "Units / day"})
fig.show()
print(f"Busiest vs. quietest weekday: {spread:.1%} difference")
```

## Shipping Performance

```{python}
shipping = q("""
    SELECT
        shipping_mode,
        COUNT(*) AS order_lines,
        ROUND(AVG(planned_ship_days), 1) AS avg_planned_days,
        ROUND(AVG(actual_ship_days), 1) AS avg_actual_days,
        ROUND(100.0 * AVG(late_delivery_risk), 1) AS late_pct
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY shipping_mode
    ORDER BY late_pct DESC
""")
shipping
```

## Late Delivery by Category

```{python}
late_by_category = q("""
    SELECT category_name, COUNT(*) AS order_lines,
           ROUND(100.0 * AVG(late_delivery_risk), 1) AS late_pct
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY category_name
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000
    ORDER BY late_pct DESC
""")
fig = px.bar(
    late_by_category, x="late_pct", y="category_name", orientation="h",
    title="Late Delivery Rate by Category (categories with 1,000+ order lines)",
    labels={"late_pct": "Late Delivery %", "category_name": "Category"},
    range_x=[0, 100],
)
fig.update_layout(yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"), height=500)
fig.show()
print(f"Range across these categories: {late_by_category['late_pct'].min()}% – "
      f"{late_by_category['late_pct'].max()}%")
```

## Do Lag Features Carry Signal?

Pooled across categories, lagged demand correlates strongly with today's demand —
but that mostly reflects categories having different *levels*. Within a single
category, the question is whether yesterday or last week says anything about today.

```{python}
corr = q(f"""
    SELECT
        CORR(lag_7d_units, total_units) AS pooled_lag7,
        (SELECT AVG(c) FROM (
            SELECT CORR(lag_7d_units, total_units) AS c
            FROM demand_features WHERE order_date <= '{MODEL_END_DATE}'
            GROUP BY category_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 365)) AS within_category_lag7,
        (SELECT AVG(c) FROM (
            SELECT CORR(lag_1d_units, total_units) AS c
            FROM demand_features WHERE order_date <= '{MODEL_END_DATE}'
            GROUP BY category_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 365)) AS within_category_lag1
    FROM demand_features
    WHERE order_date <= '{MODEL_END_DATE}'
""")
corr.round(3)
```

## Does Discounting Move Volume?

```{python}
discount = q("""
    SELECT AVG(c) AS avg_within_category_corr
    FROM (SELECT CORR(avg_discount, total_units) AS c
          FROM daily_demand WHERE NOT is_filled GROUP BY category_name)
""")
discount.round(3)
```

## Forecast Results

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("..").resolve()))
from src.forecasting.predict import list_trained_series

results = list_trained_series()
if results.empty:
    print("No trained models yet — run: python -m src.forecasting.train")
else:
    summary = results.assign(
        xgb_minus_ma28=lambda d: d["holdout_wape"] - d["holdout_wape_moving_average"]
    )[["level", "name", "champion", "holdout_wape", "holdout_wape_moving_average",
       "xgb_minus_ma28", "holdout_coverage"]]
    display(summary.round(3))
    print(f"Champion = XGBoost on {(results['champion'] == 'xgboost').sum()} of {len(results)} series; "
          f"mean 95% interval coverage {results['holdout_coverage'].mean():.0%}")
```

## Key Findings

```{python}
findings = [
    f"**Structural break:** monthly volume changes {after / before - 1:+.0%} after October 2017 "
    "as the catalog changes, so models use data up to 2017-10-02 only.",
    f"**No weekly seasonality:** the busiest and quietest weekdays differ by {spread:.1%}.",
    f"**Late deliveries depend on shipping mode, not category:** categories range only "
    f"{late_by_category['late_pct'].min()}–{late_by_category['late_pct'].max()}% late, while "
    f"{shipping.iloc[0]['shipping_mode']} is {shipping.iloc[0]['late_pct']}% late "
    f"(planned {shipping.iloc[0]['avg_planned_days']} days, actual {shipping.iloc[0]['avg_actual_days']}).",
    f"**Lags carry almost no within-category signal:** lag-7 correlation is "
    f"{corr['pooled_lag7'].iloc[0]:.2f} pooled but {corr['within_category_lag7'].iloc[0]:.2f} within a category.",
    f"**Discounts don't move daily volume:** average within-category correlation "
    f"{discount['avg_within_category_corr'].iloc[0]:.2f}.",
    "**Implication for forecasting:** demand is close to noise around a stable level, so a tuned "
    "XGBoost model can at best match a 28-day moving average — which is what the holdout results show.",
]
from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown("\n".join(f"{i}. {f}" for i, f in enumerate(findings, 1)))
```
